title: Pauri 23, sound: saalaahee saalaah
hookLine: saalaahee saalaah etee surat na paaeeaa
tomorrow: Pauri 23, meaning: the ant who remembers

cards: A superfan of a band can recite every lyric and every tour. They've been to the shows, bought the records, worn the shirts. They praise and praise.
Ask why the music moves them, though, and the answer often trails off into a shrug and a smile. The love is real; the explanation runs out. Praising something and fully grasping it aren't the same.
Pauri 23 opens with the people who praise, and a gentle, honest line about what they still don't know.

teach.b: Here's the first line, in the original: saalaahee saalaah etee surat na paaeeaa. Slowly. Saalaah, saa-LAAH: praise.
You met it in Pauri 19: akharee saalaah, through letters, praise.
Saalaahee, saa-laa-HEE: the praisers, those who praise. So saalaahee saalaah: the praisers praise, the same root twice, like an echo. Etee: this much, so much.
Surat: awareness, understanding, our word on day one hundred eighty-four, the waking attention that trust brings. Na paaeeaa: have not obtained, have not reached.
Together: the praisers praise, but have not reached an understanding of how great. Hear the music. Saalaahee saalaah is soft and flowing, the long aa like breath going out.
Then etee surat na paaeeaa tips over, as if it's shrugging.
This isn't criticism of the people who praise; Japji is full of praise.

It's the same honesty that runs through these stanzas: no pen for this, the writing runs out, only the Maker knows. Even the ones who praise most haven't grasped the size of it, and that's not a failure.
Praise doesn't need a complete understanding to be real. Tomorrow the stanza gives a picture of that: rivers, the sea, and a very small ant.

how: Pauri 23 is recited in the morning Japji Sahib; praise, saalaah, is at the center of Sikh worship, sung as kirtan in gurdwaras every day.

o: a greeting of peace, like salaam
a prayer asking God for help

games.q: the sound of Pauri 23 — tap the pairs.

s: Japji is full of praise; it only says praise hasn't grasped how great.
surat in Pauri 23 is the same word as our word on day 184
saalaah appears earlier in Japji, in Pauri 19

games.q: you've praised something your whole life. what does Pauri 23 say about your understanding of it?
o: the praisers praise, but haven't grasped how great.
you should stop praising until you understand.
games.why: saalaahee saalaah etee surat na paaeeaa. praise is real without a complete understanding.

practice: Say the line aloud, saalaahee saalaah, etee surat na paaeeaa: once slowly, letting the long aa sounds breathe out, then twice more, softer each time. Sit and listen to the quiet after the last aa fades.
Let the line keep echoing without working out what it means; that's tomorrow's job.

wordCard.voice: Saalaah, praise. It opens saalaahee saalaah, etee surat na paaeeaa: the praisers praise, but haven't grasped how great.

carryVoice: Your line: saalaahee. Admiring something doesn't have to wait until you can explain it. Until tomorrow.
